# Founding Fuel: Brand, Marketing & Storytelling — Batch 1 (2015–2020)
## Dense Observations with Full Attribution

---

## RECURRING ARGUMENTS FF MAKES

**1. Brand advocacy is superior to satisfaction or loyalty**
The hierarchy runs: satisfied customer → loyal customer → brand advocate. The ultimate goal is "customers who would not just be satisfied or loyal to my brand, but scream, shout and broadcast to everyone who cares to listen what a great brand they are using." — SOURCE: "Brand friend for life" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-22)

**2. Peer recommendation crushes advertising in credibility**
Nielsen 2009: 90% trust recommendations from people they know; 92% trust earned media (Nielsen 2012). "Advertising lacks credibility and pales before the power of friendly recommendations." Advertising spending follows the "law of diminishing returns." — SOURCE: "Brand friend for life" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-22)

**3. The product/service experience IS the marketing**
Google rejected Sergio Zyman's marketing plan and let the search engine "do the talking." "Their mantra was: Focus on the user and all else will follow." — SOURCE: "Brand friend for life" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-22)

**4. Storytelling as competitive advantage in business**
Repeated insistently across many articles. "Business storytelling is a simple and effective tool to harnesses the power of stories to connect, engage and inspire." It works in sales, marketing, leadership, strategy communication, B2B case studies, and personal branding. — SOURCE: "Once upon a time…" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-30)

**5. Stories work because of neuroscience, not sentiment**
"Speaker-Listener Neural Coupling" (Charles Gross, Princeton, 2010, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences): neurons in speaker and listener "lit up and followed a similar pattern." The listener even anticipates ahead of the teller. — SOURCE: "Once upon a time…" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-30)

**6. Character trumps credentials**
"Beyond a point, credentials do not matter as much as character does. In fact, I think character always trumps credentials." The "connection story" — a real personal anecdote — communicates character better than any résumé. — SOURCE: "Connection stories to build rapport" by Founding Fuel (2015-04-13)

**7. The Product → Service → Experience Economy progression**
A clear evolutionary framework: Product Economy (transaction, standardized), Service Economy (ready-to-consume, premium), Experience Economy (engages all five senses, creates lasting memories, emotional bonds). Starbucks as the canonical Experience Economy example. — SOURCE: "Why you should sell your brand as an experience" by Founding Fuel (2015-06-17)

**8. "Cool brands" add two dimensions beyond satisfying**
A brand satisfies; a cool brand also (a) boosts self-esteem/confidence and (b) helps the customer project themselves to peers. "A cool brand helps us shape our identity, enhance our confidence and self-esteem and helps us project ourselves to the rest of the world." BMW is the primary example. — SOURCE: "A Brand Is Not Enough. Create a Cool Brand" by Founding Fuel (2015-07-30)

**9. Consumers want to co-own brands, not just consume them**
"Today's customers are no longer satisfied being passively involved with the brand they patronize; they wish to be actively engaged." "Legally the brand belongs to the enterprise, but emotionally its ownership rests in the hearts of customers." The smartphone enabled this tectonic shift. — SOURCE: "How to get customers to own your brand" by Founding Fuel (2015-05-20)

**10. "Prosumers" — producer-consumers — drive self-regulating brand ecosystems**
Airbnb, Uber, eBay cited as models. Prosumers create user-generated reviews that are more credible than advertising and make platforms self-regulating. — SOURCE: "How to get customers to own your brand" by Founding Fuel (2015-05-20)

**11. Ads fail when they interrupt, not engage**
Five failure modes: one-way, one-sided, mass communication, not context/location optimized, putting company interest ahead of customer's. The Ronaldo penalty-kick scenario illustrates: "Many would curse your brand because it has intruded into their lives unsolicited and uninvited." — SOURCE: "Smart strategies to get customers to actively seek out your brand communication" by Founding Fuel (2015-07-15)

**12. Stories have measurable ROI**
A 3,200-word eBay story added €53,000 in value to a car — "ROI of almost Euro 17 per word." Rob Walker/Joshua Glenn's "Significant Objects" experiment: $128.74 investment yielded $3,612.51 (ROI of 2,806%). Jim Collins/Jerry Porras: purpose-driven companies outperform the market 15:1. — SOURCE: "The ROI of business storytelling" by Indranil Chakraborty (2015-12-05)

**13. Reputation management requires immediate transparency; distinguish competency vs. integrity failures**
Two categories: competency issues (honest mistakes → apologize unconditionally, likely forgiven) vs. integrity issues (knowing unethical decisions → must be penalized). Nestle/Maggi cited as integrity issue; Cadbury, PepsiCo/Coca-Cola mentioned. — SOURCE: "Reputation Management: What to Do When Your Brand Is Hit by a Scandal" by Founding Fuel (2015-08-12)

**14. Stories, not sights, make destinations worth visiting**
Taj Mahal vs. Bibi Ka Maqbara: same architectural type, 10x the visitors. The difference is the love story of Shah Jahan. "Story, somehow transforms simple stone walls into a vibrant, emotionally charged, meaningful, and exciting landscape." (Quoting Kendall Haven quoting Heisenberg/Bohr.) — SOURCE: "Stories, not places, inspire us to travel" by Indranil Chakraborty (2017-04-04)

**15. Political campaigns as storytelling laboratories**
BJP's 2019 victory analyzed as a masterclass in storytelling: "Without a well-honed storytelling approach, none of these on their own would have had the desired effect of building a committed fan base." Congress's failure attributed to failing to tell compelling stories. — SOURCE: "The BJP's real Brahmastra" by Anmol Shrivastava (2019-06-02); SOURCE: "The power of a good story" by Founding Fuel (2019-05-27)

---

## FF'S INDIA-SPECIFIC ANGLE

**IPL as the biggest brand platform in India**
Pepsi's strategy of running customer-made TV commercials during IPL — "the biggest platform in India" — to ignite brand buzz and employ "effort justification" behavioral science principle. — SOURCE: "How to get customers to own your brand" by Founding Fuel (2015-05-20)

**Paper Boat: nostalgia as India-specific brand strategy**
"A longing for simpler, uncomplicated times" tapped from Indian consumer psyche. Paper Boat explicitly positioned on "alive" (contemporary) and "authentic" (pure, natural). Shripad Nadkarni (ex-Coca-Cola India): "If you tap into a powerful human emotion, you don't need a lot of money." Own manufacturing plants to maintain recipe authenticity. — SOURCE: "Paper Boat: Riding on a wave of nostalgia" by Founding Fuel (2016-09-22)

**TikTok as Bharat phenomenon — not an urban story**
"TikTok is for the Buntys and Bablis of Bharat." 200 million Indian users. FMCG majors, broadcasters, automobile, paints and finance companies "continue to remain blissfully insulated." Influencers interviewed: a farmer, a doctor, a grandmom-grandson duo, a biker, a chef, an educator of basic English. — SOURCE: "Bharat is watching this. Is your brand watching too?" by Piyul Mukherjee (2019-07-28)

**Kanchipuram silk as MSME branding case**
A GI-protected product facing existential challenge: youngsters "voting with their feet" for automobile/electronics plants. Two competing forces — automation/commoditization vs. handcraft exclusivity. Nalli Kuppusami quoted: traditional loom meant "no more than three women could wear the same type of saree throughout the world" — exclusiveness now gone. Saris "sell auspiciousness," not just cloth; retailers won't take back sold saris because they've "lost auspiciousness." — SOURCE: "Why Kanchipuram should weave stories" by N S Ramnath (2020-07-10)

**Ramraj Cotton: solving the dhoti's image and functional problem**
Founder R. Nagarajan denied entry to 5-star hotel in a dhoti → built brand on inverting that humiliation. Velcro dhoti solves the "slip" pain point. Damodar Mall (Reliance Retail CEO) publicly endorsed it. "Find a pain point…solve it, and people will not only beat the streets to buy it, they will also endorse it." — SOURCE: "How to brand a humble piece of white cloth" by N S Ramnath (2020-07-18)

**BJP as political storytelling case — with explicit Steve Jobs comparison**
Jobs's "Think Different" campaign compared directly to BJP's storytelling apparatus. Steve Jobs quote opens the article: "The most powerful person in the world is the storyteller." Modi as hero-figure: "one of every three of those who voted for the BJP said that they would have voted differently had Modi not been the prime ministerial candidate." — SOURCE: "The BJP's real Brahmastra" by Anmol Shrivastava (2019-06-02)

**HUL's social media brand crisis — analyzed through Goffman**
Red Label Kumbh Mela ad and Surf Excel Holi ad failures interpreted using Erving Goffman's "Presentation of Self in Everyday Life" (1956). "All the web's a stage, and all men and women are alert members of the audience gunning for the next victim." India-specific: Kalyan Jewellers + Amitabh Bachchan ad also cited. — SOURCE: "Hindustan Unilever's storm in a teacup" by Piyul Mukherjee (2019-03-08)

**Gandhi's Salt March as publicity masterclass for entrepreneurs**
Five lessons: broad audience appeal, ease of participation, dramatic scripting in acts, media priming, strategic ambiguity forcing adversary dilemma. "Gandhi's choice to defy the salt law seemed strange and harmless. The British viceroy Lord Irwin wrote to London, 'At present the prospect of a salt campaign does not keep me awake at night.'" — SOURCE: "Five publicity lessons Mahatma Gandhi teaches entrepreneurs" by Baba Prasad (2018-04-13)

**Taj vs. Bibi Ka Maqbara: Indian monument data**
Taj Mahal draws ~68 lakh visitors/year (20% foreign); Bibi Ka Maqbara draws ~6.6 lakh (2% foreign). The difference is purely the story attached. Government of India Tourism statistics cited. — SOURCE: "Stories, not places, inspire us to travel" by Indranil Chakraborty (2017-04-04)

**Asian brands historically underinvest in marketing**
"Many Asian firms, at least historically, have believed that marketing somehow would just come from the bottom up. But I believe that if you want to become an Apple, if you want to become a BMW, then marketing has to come center stage." — Martin Roll, quoted. — SOURCE: "How to create your product differentiation strategy" by CKGSB Knowledge (2017-02-14)

**Hidesign: authentic brand-building from Aurobindo Ashram roots**
Dilip Kapur says he "simply made what he liked, without a thought about whether somebody else would like them." When you start thinking too much about what someone likes, "you end up designing 'safe' products." CSR tied to brand values: wildlife, ecology, medicinal herbs. — SOURCE: "Why talking about who you are is key to building your brand" by Founding Fuel (2015-05-07)

**Fake Twitter followers in India — exposed with recorded audio**
Rs 400 for 1,000 "cheap" followers (not guaranteed to stay). Rs 3,000 for 1,000 manually created Indian handles. Previous attempts via Bangladesh-based sweatshops. Twitter India spokesperson noted algorithms cull fake followers. Twitter Audit applied to five top Indian politicians and businessmen. — SOURCE: "How to buy friends and influence people" by Charles Assisi (2015-05-10)

**E-commerce branding vacuum in India**
E-commerce players "pumped in approximately Rs 1,000 crore of advertisement money across media channels in 2014" (FICCI-KPMG report) — all on undifferentiated platforms. "Firms are not thinking branding yet. For them, it simply implies advertising." The word "phygital" coined to describe omni-channel convergence. — SOURCE: "Designing a sharply positioned platform" by Amrita Chowdhury (2016-06-03)

---

## FRAMEWORKS, THINKERS, AND MENTAL MODELS

**Joseph Campbell's Hero's Journey (1949) — explicitly rejected for business storytelling**
"Many business managers I meet think that for their stories to work, they need to be big and grand and follow the Hero's Journey plot line." FF argues against this. Small 's' vs. Big 'S' storytelling continuum. — SOURCE: "Business Storytelling is Not About the Hero's Journey" by Founding Fuel (2015-08-07)

**Carl Jung's archetypes** — referenced in relation to Hero's Journey framework — SOURCE: "Business Storytelling is Not About the Hero's Journey" by Founding Fuel (2015-08-07)

**Speaker-Listener Neural Coupling (Charles Gross, Princeton, 2010)**
Neurons in speaker and listener follow similar patterns; listener anticipates ahead of the teller. — SOURCE: "Once upon a time…" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-30)

**Annette Simmons, "Whoever Tells the Best Story Wins"**
"People won't listen to you until they know who you are and what you want." — SOURCE: "Connection stories to build rapport" by Founding Fuel (2015-04-13)

**Erving Goffman, "The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life" (1956)**
Dramaturgical model: front stage/backstage, social embarrassment avoidance. Applied to brand communication in age of social media: "all the web's a stage, and all men and women are alert members of the audience gunning for the next victim." — SOURCE: "Hindustan Unilever's storm in a teacup" by Piyul Mukherjee (2019-03-08)

**Jim Collins & Jerry Porras, "Built to Last"**
Purpose-driven companies outperform market 15:1 and comparison companies 6:1. — SOURCE: "The ROI of business storytelling" by Indranil Chakraborty (2015-12-05)

**John Kotter & James Heskett, "Corporate Culture and Performance"**
Companies with purpose-and-values cultures show revenue growth 4x faster, share price growth 12x faster. — SOURCE: "The ROI of business storytelling" by Indranil Chakraborty (2015-12-05)

**Daniel Kahneman — "The Riddle of Experience vs. Memory" (2010 TED Talk)**
Experiencing self vs. remembering self. "A dreadful screeching sound at the end of the recording ruined the whole experience" — but it hadn't. It ruined the memories. Crucial for tourism/destination marketing argument. — SOURCE: "Stories, not places, inspire us to travel" by Indranil Chakraborty (2017-04-04)

**Rob Walker & Joshua Glenn — "Significant Objects" experiment (2009)**
$128.74 in thrift store objects + invented stories → $3,612.51 on eBay (2,806% ROI). — SOURCE: "The ROI of business storytelling" by Indranil Chakraborty (2015-12-05)

**Shawn Callahan (Anecdote, Australia) — story-based organizational change**
Credited as Indranil Chakraborty's partner/mentor. Gandhi's "Be the change you want to see" applied to persuading leaders to adopt storytelling

# Founding Fuel: Brand, Marketing & Storytelling — Batch 2 Observations

## ARGUMENTS FF MAKES REPEATEDLY

**Storytelling as the primary instrument of persuasion and change**
- The Sameer Bhatia bone marrow story illustrates that "He chose the latter. He shared the story about Sameer in a way that was so personal rather than analytical that anyone who read it or heard it felt connected to Sameer." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #358: How a good story gets a tough job done" by Founding Fuel (2021-04-28)
- Wilson's anthropological evidence: "Storytelling... consumed 6% of the overall recorded time during the day, but they consumed 81% of the evening" — SOURCE: "FF Daily #345: Why and when we tell stories" by Founding Fuel (2021-04-13)
- Anderson's contrast of good vs. bad storytelling: "The second version is a mess. The drama is killed by revealing the father's intent too early" — SOURCE: "FF Daily #497: How to tell a good story" by Founding Fuel (2021-10-14)

**Show, don't tell as a core persuasion principle**
- The pizza app founder: "though the slides were well designed and the content was strong, his delivery fell flat" — slides fail, live demonstration succeeds — SOURCE: "FF Daily #459: Why show not tell matters" by Founding Fuel (2021-08-26)

**Authenticity over polish in communication**
- Terry Szuplat/Obama: "the most effective public speakers are those who know who they are, what they believe in, and speak with clarity and conviction. Audiences can sense when you don't truly believe in your own words." — SOURCE: "Terry Szuplat on the Art of Powerful Communication" by Founding Fuel (2025-09-26)

**Purpose must be operational, not decorative**
- "Purpose here does not sit on a wall. It shapes behaviour, credibility and, ultimately, impact." — SOURCE: "The Quiet Work of Branding" by Indranil Gupta (2026-01-13)
- "Purpose has moved decisively beyond slogans and CSR pages." — SOURCE: "The Quiet Work of Branding" by Indranil Gupta (2026-01-13)

**Branding as sense-making during transitions, not cosmetic exercise**
- "branding can no longer be cosmetic. It has to help organisations orient themselves before they can persuade others." — SOURCE: "The Quiet Work of Branding" by Indranil Gupta (2026-01-13)
- "The most productive conversations I've seen begin when leaders stop asking, 'How do we look?' and start asking, 'What problem do we exist to solve now—and for whom?'" — SOURCE: "The Quiet Work of Branding" by Indranil Gupta (2026-01-13)

**Simplicity as deliberate compression, not mere reduction**
- Lincoln's Gettysburg Address: "With just 272 words, it is one of the shortest ever written. Delivered in just about two minutes, it changed the course of America's political history." — SOURCE: "FF Life: How to write better" by Founding Fuel (2022-01-31)
- Apple's Jonathan Ive cited: "Simplicity is not the absence of clutter, that's a consequence of simplicity. Simplicity is somehow essentially describing the purpose and place of an object and product." — SOURCE: "FF Life: A beginner's guide to graphic novels" by N S Ramnath (2024-05-03)

**Campaigns are insufficient; narrative platforms are necessary**
- "One-off campaigns are steadily giving way to something more cumulative... When conversations, events, publications, learning cohorts and recognitions are stitched together with intent, they begin to form a narrative platform." — SOURCE: "The Quiet Work of Branding" by Indranil Gupta (2026-01-13)

**Personal brand is no longer optional in professional life**
- "In today's professional world, you are on your own—in your career, in your life and hence the need to build your personal brand for success." — SOURCE: "A personal brand is a must" by D Shivakumar (2023-05-01)
- "In the past personal branding was what you said about yourself, today, it is the intersection of what you say about yourself and what others say about you." — SOURCE: "A personal brand is a must" by D Shivakumar (2023-05-01)

**Digital's "always on" nature creates pressure that distorts creative judgment**
- "Digital is 'always on' and eyeball opportunities have to be captured fast and on the go. Hence the constant need to push creative boundaries and create brand content that gets immediate attention." — SOURCE: "Creative marketing in the digital age: How far is too far?" by Vivek Sharma (2024-02-15)

**Listening before speaking is leadership discipline**
- Aditya Ghosh: "I've never done a customer survey in my life. But I've done hundreds of employee surveys and thousands of interactions with colleagues." — SOURCE: "FF Live: Managing Corporate Reputation in the Digital Age" by Founding Fuel (2025-03-06)
- David Ogilvy invoked: "big ears rather than big mouths" — SOURCE: "FF Live: Managing Corporate Reputation in the Digital Age" by Founding Fuel (2025-03-06)

---

## FF'S INDIA-SPECIFIC ANGLE

**India's vernacular literary ecosystem as an underrepresented cultural asset**
- Salman Rushdie's 1997 anthology featured no writer from Indian languages; 2022 Booker to Geetanjali Shree marks a turning point: "India has come a long way since the time Rushdie published The Vintage Book of Indian Writing." — SOURCE: "FF Life: The best translated works from Indian languages" by Founding Fuel (2022-06-11)
- "To understand India, you have to read the books written in Indian languages, the languages in which people think, feel and dream." — SOURCE: "FF Life: The best translated works from Indian languages" by Founding Fuel (2022-06-11)

**India's diaspora as authentic brand originators, not cultural exploiters**
- Aavrani's Rooshy Roy: "these are just ingredients I grew up with" vs. Western appropriation framing of Indian adaptogens — SOURCE: "An Indian beauty upstart in the West" by Aparajita Bhattacharyya (2021-05-31)
- Aavrani deliberately contrasts with "fetishizing of desi culture (I'm looking at you Slumdog Millionaire)" — SOURCE: "Ms Marvel is an important cultural event, and you don't even know about it" by Ronaan Roy (2022-07-03)

**India's beauty/consumer market inverting the legacy brand logic**
- Sugar Cosmetics: "Legacy brands thought that the product is a commodity and the Rs 100 crore they spend on marketing is their moat. We turned that around on its head—if you have a hero product, social media and e-commerce will ensure that it gets discovered." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #547: Success can't be taken for granted" by Founding Fuel (2021-12-18)
- Sugar achieves 400 million+ monthly views through "earned and owned media, instead of paid media (which legacy brands typically deploy)." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #547: Success can't be taken for granted" by Founding Fuel (2021-12-18)

**Indians as "conservative" drinkers and the challenge of cocktail culture**
- "Our observations and anecdotal evidence suggest that Indians are not big on cocktails. Most people are 'conservative' drinkers who stick to their whiskey, rum." — SOURCE: "FF Life: Hakuna Ma'vodka!" by Founding Fuel (2022-12-16)
- Meenakshi Menon: "Indians are big on sweet cocktails if at all they experiment and it's such an insult to good liquor to drown it in fruit juice." — SOURCE: "FF Life: Hakuna Ma'vodka!" by Founding Fuel (2022-12-16)

**India's wine market stratification — old money vs. new tastes**
- Vishal Kadakia's clientele: "above the age of 40, who often travel abroad, have a high disposable income and can tell the difference between a Burgundy and a Bordeaux" vs. "millennials and Gen Z lapping up Indian whiskies, gins, craft beers." — SOURCE: "FF Life: One sip at a time" by Aayush Soni (2023-09-22)

**Indian governance context for digital crisis management**
- Sabia Schwarzer's advice gets India-localised: "Who are the officials in your city who are involved in [policing] cybercrime." — SOURCE: "FF Live: Managing Corporate Reputation in the Digital Age" by Founding Fuel (2025-03-06)

**Poonam Pandey stunt as specifically Indian marketing failure case study**
- FF frames it as raising systemic questions for "the marketing industry" about governance and accountability — SOURCE: "Creative marketing in the digital age: How far is too far?" by Vivek Sharma (2024-02-15)

**Kolkata's Durga Puja as world-class cultural storytelling event**
- Positioned as "the world's largest street art and installation festival" with UNESCO recognition, meriting annual FF coverage and curation — SOURCE: "Curtain Raiser: The Durga Puja Experience in Kolkata" by Founding Fuel (2025-09-14)

---

## FRAMEWORKS, THINKERS, AND MENTAL MODELS

**Jennifer Aaker's Dragonfly Effect framework for change-making stories**
- Four elements: Focus, Grab Attention, Engage, Take Action — SOURCE: "FF Daily #358: How a good story gets a tough job done" by Founding Fuel (2021-04-28)

**Edward O. Wilson on evolutionary origins of storytelling**
- Campfire thesis: daytime talk is practical, firelight talk is narrative and communal — SOURCE: "FF Daily #345: Why and when we tell stories" by Founding Fuel (2021-04-13)

**Chris Anderson (TED) on story architecture**
- Character + drama + resolution vs. intent-revealing, detail-cluttered anti-pattern — SOURCE: "FF Daily #497: How to tell a good story" by Founding Fuel (2021-10-14)

**Suneel Gupta's "Backable" principle: show vs. tell**
- Cited as central to persuasion in pitching and presenting — SOURCE: "FF Daily #459: Why show not tell matters" by Founding Fuel (2021-08-26)

**Mortimer Adler's reading hierarchy**
- Elementary → Inspectional → Analytical reading as foundation for writing well — SOURCE: "FF Life: How to write better" by Founding Fuel (2022-01-31)

**Schopenhauer's warning on passive reading**
- "When we read, another person thinks for us: we merely repeat his mental process." — SOURCE: "FF Life: How to write better" by Founding Fuel (2022-01-31)

**Stephen King and Roy Peter Clark as writing craft authorities**
- Invoked repeatedly for practical writing tools — SOURCE: "FF Life: How to write better" by Founding Fuel (2022-01-31)

**Scott McCloud's "Understanding Comics" on visual simplification**
- Cited for the principle of stripping to essential meaning — SOURCE: "FF Life: A beginner's guide to graphic novels" by N S Ramnath (2024-05-03)

**Jim Collins' "How the Mighty Fall" on institutional vulnerability**
- Bank of America as cautionary tale: "Every institution is vulnerable, no matter how great." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #547: Success can't be taken for granted" by Founding Fuel (2021-12-18)

**Sangeet Paul Choudary's Web2/Web3 market governance unbundling**
- Infrastructure vs. governance as separate layers — SOURCE: "FF Daily #459: Why show not tell matters" by Founding Fuel (2021-08-26)

**Indranil Gupta's five branding shifts framework**
- Sense-making → Purpose as operating logic → Narrative platforms → Co-creation → Trust — SOURCE: "The Quiet Work of Branding" by Indranil Gupta (2026-01-13)

**Freakonomics' Superman/KKK example**
- Mass media dismantling prejudice through cultural infiltration — SOURCE: "Ms Marvel is an important cultural event" by Ronaan Roy (2022-07-03)

**Mary Meeker / Benedict Evans deck tradition**
- Held as standard for presentation excellence — SOURCE: "FF Life: How to make beautiful presentations" by N S Ramnath (2022-05-02)

---

## WHAT FF IS SKEPTICAL OF / PUSHES BACK AGAINST

**PR stunts that manufacture emotion around serious social issues**
- "The Poonam Pandey-cervical cancer episode is in a series of many others earlier... a blatant manipulation of their emotions" — SOURCE: "Creative marketing in the digital age: How far is too far?" by Vivek Sharma (2024-02-15)

**Legacy brands' reliance on paid marketing spend as the primary moat**
- Sugar Cosmetics inverted this: the Rs 100 crore marketing spend was the legacy moat, not the product — SOURCE: "FF Daily #547: Success can't be taken for granted" by Founding Fuel (2021-12-18)

**PowerPoint as default communication format (nuanced — not absolute rejection)**
- Amazon/Bezos memo culture acknowledged; but FF defends decks "when done well" — SOURCE: "FF Life: How to make beautiful presentations" by N S Ramnath (2022-05-02)

**Anonymous complaints and social media noise as management input**
- Aditya Ghosh: "I do not give any credence to anonymous emails." — SOURCE: "FF Live: Managing Corporate Reputation in the Digital Age" by Founding Fuel (2025-03-06)

**Quantity of books read over quality of engagement**
- "Most people place a premium on the number of books read as opposed to wrestling with the ideas in a book." — SOURCE: "FF Life: How to write better" by Founding Fuel (2022-01-31)

**Oscar politics and prestige-bait filmmaking**
- Ronaan Roy on CODA: "it will be glossed over" — SOURCE: "FF Life: The Oscar Rosters 2023" by Ronaan Roy (2023-03-03)
- On Maestro: "tasting more of Oscar Bait than anything else" — SOURCE: "FF Life: The Oscar Rosters 2024" by Ronaan Roy (2024-03-08)
- On Elvis: "greatly simplifies a complex narrative by giving the film a villain" — SOURCE: "FF Life: The Oscar Rosters 2023" by Ronaan Roy (2023-03-03)

**Western cultural mainstream's neglect of South Asian representation**
- Ms. Marvel's low viewership despite 96% Rotten Tomatoes score — "instead of catching and celebrating her, they parted like Musa's red sea" — SOURCE: "Ms Marvel is an important cultural event" by Ronaan Roy (2022-07-03)

**The fetishization of desi culture by Western media**
- "Unlike the fetishizing of desi culture (I'm looking at you Slumdog Millionaire)" — SOURCE: "Ms Marvel is an important cultural event" by Ronaan Roy (2022-07-03)

**AI replacing human voice in communication**
- "when it comes to expressing your vision and values, only a human voice can inspire and move people. In an AI-saturated world, audiences will crave authentic, human-led moments even more." — SOURCE: "Terry Szuplat on the Art of Powerful Communication" by Founding Fuel (2025-09-26)

**Surface-level purpose statements**
- "Purpose has moved decisively beyond slogans and CSR pages." — SOURCE: "The Quiet Work of Branding" by Indranil Gupta (2026-01-13)

**Paid awards as personal brand builders**
- "There are many paid awards—avoid them. The more paid awards you have the less credible your personal brand." — SOURCE: "A personal brand is a must" by D Shivakumar (2023-05-01)

---

## COMPANIES, LEADERS, OR EXAMPLES FF CELEBRATES OR CRITIQUES

**Celebrated:**
- **Sugar Cosmetics / Vineeta Singh**: Product obsession + earned media model vs. paid media dependency — SOURCE: "FF Daily #547: Success can't be taken for
